headline: Visiting the Iconic Peggy's Point Lighthouse
reservation: Peggy's Cove is a public scenic area and a working fishing village with no entry fee or reservation required for the village itself. However, parking is limited and tour bus schedules can create significant congestion; verify local traffic advisories during the peak cruise ship season.

days.title: Granite Coast and Fishing Heritage

stops.name: Peggy's Point Lighthouse
stops.detail: View the most famous lighthouse in Canada set against massive white granite boulders.

stops.name: William E. deGarthe Memorial Provincial Park
stops.detail: See the impressive stone carving depicting the lives of local fishermen directly in the village.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours from Halifax; conditions vary with fog and narrow coastal roads.
days.note: Stay off the 'black rocks' near the water; rogue waves are a serious and frequent hazard.

days.title: St. Margarets Bay Scenic Drive

stops.name: Swissair Flight 111 Memorial
stops.detail: Visit the peaceful commemorative site at Whalesback, offering a somber moment and ocean views.

stops.name: Polly's Cove
stops.detail: Hike the rugged coastal barrens just down the road for a view of the lighthouse from a distance.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 to 2 hours from Lunenburg; conditions vary along the Lighthouse Route.
days.note: The terrain at Polly's Cove is uneven and rocky; allow extra time for foot travel.

days.title: Coastal Barrens and Inlets

stops.name: West Dover Provincial Park
stops.detail: Explore the unique 'barrens' ecosystem characterized by low-lying shrubs and erratic boulders.

stops.name: Indian Harbour
stops.detail: Stop at this nearby working cove to see traditional dories and lobster traps in a less crowded setting.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours from Dartmouth; conditions vary with seasonal construction.
days.note: Infrastructure in the village is historic and narrow; be prepared for slow vehicle movement.

intel.title: Visitor Information Centre Lots
intel.text: Primary parking is available at the entrance to the village; avoid driving into the narrow residential lanes. On busy summer afternoons, these lots often fill, requiring a wait for departing visitors.

intel.title: Unreliable Coastal Roaming
intel.text: Cell service is generally available but can be spotty among the granite ridges and inland coastal barrens. Do not rely solely on streaming GPS for navigation on the backroads of the South Shore.

intel.title: Upper Tantallon Hub
intel.text: The last major service hub for fuel and groceries is located in Upper Tantallon at the junction of Highway 103 and Route 333. There are no gas stations in the immediate village of Peggy's Cove.

intel.title: Fog and Visibility
intel.text: Coastal fog can move in rapidly, obscuring the lighthouse even when it is sunny inland. Check the local maritime weather forecast if the lighthouse view is your primary goal.

intel.title: Accessible Viewing Deck
intel.text: A recently constructed accessible wooden boardwalk provides a safe viewing platform near the lighthouse. This allows visitors with mobility challenges to experience the rocks without navigating the uneven granite.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at Halifax Stanfield International Airport (YHZ) and drive approximately 75 minutes via Highway 103 and Route 333 to reach the coast.
plan.vehicle: A compact or mid-size car is recommended for navigating the very tight turns within the village; large RVs are discouraged from entering the village core.
plan.goldenHour: The view of the lighthouse from the granite boulders at sunset is iconic, but shadows lengthen early in the narrow coves; check local seasonal sunset times.
